measures: Whether the document survives a six-second recruiter scan and reads as edited prose.
source: Criteria drafted for ticket 12 against the category 04 defined. Not corpus-derived and cannot be: the postings describe the job, not the resume, so this category has no document frequency and an authored weight. The five criteria are what survives subtracting the ~40 deterministic rules 07 files here -- see resume-craft-criteria.md section 'The subtraction'.

criteria.name: says what it is
criteria.question: Does the resume say what this person is, above the first role, rather than leaving the reader to infer it from a job title?
criteria.yes_requires: A quote above the first role naming the discipline -- a summary line or a role line. 'AI Engineer, 3 yrs -- LLM serving and evals.'
criteria.no_looks_like: A name, an email, and straight into a job. The reader has to read a bullet before knowing what they are looking at.

criteria.name: names what changed
criteria.question: Does every role have at least one bullet naming something that is different because of the work?
criteria.yes_requires: One quote per role stating a change -- something cut, raised, replaced, unblocked, shipped. Not the assignment, the difference.
criteria.no_looks_like: A role whose bullets are all responsibilities: 'Responsible for maintaining the pipeline', 'Worked on model architectures', 'Involved in the migration'.

criteria.name: says what it was for
criteria.question: Does the resume say what the work was for -- a product, a user, a problem -- rather than only the stack and the number?
criteria.yes_requires: A quote naming the thing the work served. 'for ticket triage', 'so support agents could answer without escalating'.
criteria.no_looks_like: Every bullet is a technology and a metric with no subject. 'Cut p99 latency 380ms to 95ms with vLLM' -- for what, and who noticed?

criteria.name: roles read differently
criteria.question: Does each role read as a different job, rather than the same work described again?
criteria.yes_requires: The roles differ in what they claim -- different systems, different scope, different problems. One role is enough to satisfy this.
criteria.no_looks_like: Two roles whose bullets are interchangeable, or a promotion where only the title changed.

criteria.name: could not be anyone's
criteria.question: Is every bullet specific enough that it could not move unchanged to a stranger's resume?
criteria.yes_requires: No bullet survives having its names, numbers and tools stripped and still saying something.
criteria.no_looks_like: 'Leveraged cutting-edge AI technologies to deliver robust and scalable solutions' -- true of anyone who has ever been employed.

bands.label: E
bands.name: Not written for a reader
bands.reads: Nothing about the document is aimed at the person reading it.

bands.label: D
bands.name: Needs a rewrite
bands.reads: Two of the five hold. The rest is a draft.

bands.label: C
bands.name: Readable, unedited
bands.reads: A reader can follow it and will notice what was left in.

bands.label: B
bands.name: One thing left
bands.reads: Edited, with one criterion still unmet -- and the report can name which.

bands.label: A
bands.name: Edited
bands.reads: It says what it is, what changed, what it was for, that the jobs differed, and none of it could be anyone else's.
